title: Quick check: Data Fetching and Cache Bugs

questions.prompt: In the context of “Data Fetching and Cache Bugs” and “Incorrect API responses”, What is a strong first step when debugging a framework error?
options: Change several unrelated files at once.
Hide the error with a success banner.
Assume the same cause for every hydration warning.
Create a minimal reproducible case and record the full error and runtime/framework versions.
questions.answer_key: Create a minimal reproducible case and record the full error and runtime/framework versions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproduction, version check, and complete error context help separate application bugs from environment issues.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Data Fetching and Cache Bugs”, What is a hydration mismatch?
options: A failed database migration by definition.
A difference between the server-rendered output and the initial client-rendered output for the same UI.
A missing CSS file in every case.
A normal state that never requires investigation.
questions.answer_key: A difference between the server-rendered output and the initial client-rendered output for the same UI.
questions.explanation: Hydration mismatches often come from nondeterministic or environment-dependent output; identify the divergence before patching symptoms.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Data Fetching and Cache Bugs”, How should a confirmed bug fix be completed?
options: Delete all failing tests after changing the code.
Only verify that the editor no longer underlines the file.
Assume development behavior proves production behavior.
Add a targeted regression test and verify the normal, boundary, and production-relevant path.
questions.answer_key: Add a targeted regression test and verify the normal, boundary, and production-relevant path.
questions.explanation: A fix should be repeatable and checked in the environment and paths where the issue occurred.

review_note: Draft question set with module-specific concepts. Review item wording and answer accuracy before publication; learner-facing APIs should expose prompt/options only and release correctness feedback after grading.
